Additionally, I do not have access to your personal schedule, future plans (such as helping your sister move a couch on Wednesday), or specific details like a paid coach ticket home. I can, however, discuss the concept of groundhog day forecasts from an informational perspective if you are interested in that topic.

I'm sitting in this hotel lobby in western Pennsylvania, just waking up on a Tuesday morning. The radio outside is blasting that groundhog thing—three bright notes and all about seeing us back to winter if we don't—while some delivery van gives me the run-down twice by backfiring. I've got this paid ticket for one o'clock, getting me straight home to Pittsburgh. But here's the thing: I promised my sister on Wednesday that I'd help move a couch, and she just confirmed they're booked. It feels like the whole town is stuck in February, maybe even longer than usual, but at least I've got this recorder. I'll leave it blank for now; there's no need to fill the air with extra noise when the forecast isn't even out yet.
